description: Enhance the dictionary engine and dataset: meaningfully expand the CC0 seed corpus, improve search relevance and scalability, and expand automated test coverage. This is the core 'reenhance' work on the search side. Depends on FEAT-001 (green baseline).
steps: Expand the seed dataset in scripts/gen-seed.mjs by adding a substantial batch of NEW original CC0 Bangla entries (target roughly doubling the corpus, e.g. from 180 to ~350+ entries) covering additional everyday vocabulary (verbs, adjectives, numbers, body parts, food, nature, kinship, time, common phrases). Every field MUST be original content written for WordSetu (CC0) — do NOT copy from any copyrighted dictionary. Follow the exact existing row tuple shape [id, headword(bn), roman, pos, ipa, defBn, defEn, synonyms[], example|null] and keep ids unique ASCII slugs. Then regenerate with `node scripts/gen-seed.mjs`, which overwrites resources/dictionary/entries.json. Keep the DictionaryFile shape (version, language 'bn-en', entries). Update SCHEMA.md only if the schema itself changes (it should not).

Confirm the regenerated entries.json still loads: the loader validates ids are unique and every entry has a non-empty headword and at least one sense with definitionBn. Fix any duplicate-id or validation problems introduced.

Improve search scalability in src/main/dictionary/engine.ts: the review flagged the fuzzy pass as an O(entries x query) full scan over every headword (boundedLevenshtein against all sortedHeadwords). Add a cheap prefilter so fuzzy only compares candidates whose length is within fuzzyThreshold of the query length (length-bucketing) and/or that share a leading character, before running boundedLevenshtein. Preserve existing ranking/score semantics and result ordering for the current test expectations — this is an internal optimization, not a behavior change. If a length/first-char prefilter would change results, keep it conservative so exact/prefix/substring/cross-language/fuzzy ordering is unchanged.

Review the cross-language English search path (searchEnglish in engine.ts) together with the ENGLISH_STOP_WORDS filter in loader.ts. Confirm stop-word pollution is handled; if any high-frequency non-stop tokens still over-match on the larger corpus, tighten the skip list or down-weight single-token cross-language matches (a match on a single common content token should not outrank multi-token or exact-gloss hits). Keep the change minimal and covered by a test.

Add/extend engine tests in tests/engine.test.ts to cover: (a) the larger corpus loads without validation errors and size is the new count; (b) fuzzy prefilter still returns the expected did-you-mean candidate for a near-miss query and does NOT change the ranking of an exact vs transliterated vs cross-language match; (c) a cross-language query on a common content word ranks the exact-gloss entry above incidental multi-entry matches. Assertions must exercise real engine behavior against the actual seed file (follow the existing pattern of loading resources/dictionary/entries.json).

Add loader tests in tests/loader.test.ts if not already covered: assert ENGLISH_STOP_WORDS tokens are excluded from englishIndex and that indexableEnglishTokens falls back to the full token list when a gloss is all stop-words.

Bump the app version from 0.1.0 to 0.2.0 in BOTH package.json ('version') and src/shared/constants.ts (APP_VERSION), since expanding the corpus and search behavior is a release-worthy change. Keep them identical. Confirm electron-builder artifactName remains WordSetu-Setup-${version}.${ext} (it references ${version} so it stays consistent automatically).
acceptance_criteria: resources/dictionary/entries.json is regenerated from scripts/gen-seed.mjs and contains a meaningfully larger set of entries (target ~350+), all with unique ids and valid schema
npm test passes including new engine/loader tests that assert the larger corpus loads and that ranking of exact vs transliterated vs cross-language is unchanged
The fuzzy search path uses a length/first-char prefilter and still returns correct did-you-mean results
package.json version and src/shared/constants.ts APP_VERSION are both 0.2.0 and identical
npm run typecheck, npm run lint, and npm run build all exit 0
findings: Expanded seed corpus from 180 to 350 original CC0 entries in scripts/gen-seed.mjs (new batches: numbers, kinship, body parts, animals, nature, food/drink, time words, verbs, adjectives, abstract concepts, places, function words). Fixed one duplicate id ('tok' -> renamed the sour-taste entry to 'tok_sour'; the skin entry keeps 'tok'). Regenerated resources/dictionary/entries.json (350 entries, unique ids, all valid slugs, loads with no DictionaryValidationError). Added a conservative length + first-char prefilter to the fuzzy pass in engine.ts (skips headwords whose length differs from the query by more than fuzzyThreshold, and for queries longer than the budget requires a reachable leading-char overlap) — purely an optimization, ranking/ordering unchanged (all prior tests still green). Cross-language exact-gloss handling already down-weights incidental single-token matches via the +200 exact-gloss bonus; verified on the larger corpus (e.g. 'old' ranks পুরনো above বৃদ্ধ) and covered by a new test. Stop-word handling in loader.ts already correct; existing loader tests cover exclusion + fallback. Added engine tests (larger-corpus load/size=350, fuzzy prefilter did-you-mean, exact vs transliterated vs cross-language tier ordering, cross-language exact-gloss priority) and tightened the loader corpus-size assertion to >=350. Bumped version 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0 in package.json and src/shared/constants.ts (APP_VERSION), electron-builder artifactName still WordSetu-Setup-${version}.${ext}. Verification all green: node scripts/gen-seed.mjs, npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm test (6 suites / 68 tests, up from 63), npm run build, npm run package:linux (dictionary copied to release/linux-unpacked/resources/resources/dictionary/entries.json with 350 entries). NOTE: the Windows .exe cannot be produced on this Linux sandbox; it is built only by .github/workflows/build-windows.yml on windows-latest (or npm run package:win on Windows).
